stories.headline: Bank of Japan Holds Rates at 0.75% in 6-3 Split Vote, Raises Inflation Forecast to 2.8%

key_facts.fact: The BOJ kept its short-term policy rate at 0.75% in a split 6-3 vote, with three board members dissenting in favor of a rate hike to 1.0%.
The BOJ raised its inflation forecast to 2.8% for fiscal year 2026, while downgrading its GDP growth forecast.
The 6-3 split marks the most hawkish divide of the Ueda era, boosting chances of a June rate hike.
Middle Eastern conflicts affecting oil prices are adding inflationary pressure to Japan's economy, cited as a key factor in the BOJ's cautious approach.
The yen steadied after the decision, having firmed initially, while the dollar edged higher as central banks remained in focus.

stories.headline: EU Unveils DMA Proposals to Force Google to Open Android to Rival AI Services

key_facts.fact: EU antitrust regulators unveiled new proposals under the Digital Markets Act aimed at opening Google's Android ecosystem to rivals' AI services on Monday April 27.
The measures target Google's AI integration with Android, aiming to let users choose alternative AI assistants and services on their devices.
Google said the EU measures are 'unwarranted intervention' in the Android ecosystem.

stories.headline: GitHub Copilot Moving to Usage-Based Billing on June 1, Replacing Premium Requests With AI Credits

key_facts.fact: All GitHub Copilot plans will transition to usage-based billing on June 1, 2026, replacing premium request units with GitHub AI Credits based on token consumption
Base plan pricing remains unchanged: Pro $10/month, Pro+ $39/month, Business $19/user/month, Enterprise $39/user/month, with equivalent monthly AI Credits included
GitHub cited that the current premium request model is no longer sustainable as Copilot evolved from an in-editor assistant into an agentic platform with much higher compute demands
Code completions and Next Edit suggestions remain included in all plans and do not consume AI Credits; fallback experiences to lower-cost models will no longer be available
Annual Pro and Pro+ subscribers are grandfathered into the existing plan until expiration, but model multipliers increase on June 1 — Claude Opus 4.7 goes from 7.5x to 27x
Enterprise customers get promotional credits for June-August: Business $30/month, Enterprise $70/month in AI Credits, with new pooled usage across organizations

stories.headline: 600+ Google Employees Including DeepMind Staff Demand Pichai Bar Pentagon From Using AI on Classified Work

key_facts.fact: More than 600 Google employees signed an open letter to CEO Sundar Pichai demanding he bar the Pentagon from using Google's AI for classified work
Signers span Google DeepMind, Cloud and other divisions, including more than 20 directors, senior directors and vice presidents
Google reportedly signed a deal allowing the US DOD to use Google's AI for 'any lawful government purpose'; the Pentagon pushed for broader 'all lawful uses' wording

The protest is the largest internal Google dissent in years, exceeding the anti-Israel protests and echoing the 2018 Project Maven controversy that led Google to withdraw from a drone footage AI program

Google has proposed contractual language preventing Gemini from being used for domestic mass surveillance or autonomous weapons without human control, but employees say safeguards would be hard to enforce

stories.headline: Ex-DeepMind's David Silver Raises Record $1.1B Seed at $5.1B Valuation for Ineffable Intelligence

key_facts.fact: Ineffable Intelligence, founded by ex-Google DeepMind Principal Scientist David Silver (creator of AlphaGo), raised $1.1B in seed funding at a $5.1B valuation
The round includes participation from Nvidia, Google, Sequoia, and the UK Sovereign AI Fund, making it one of the largest seed rounds ever recorded
The London-based company is focused on developing 'superlearner' AI systems based on reinforcement learning that learn autonomously through experience, without relying on human-generated data
The company was founded in late 2025 and is headquartered in London, marking a milestone for Europe's AI ecosystem
Nvidia announced a collaboration with Ineffable Intelligence, with more details to come

stories.headline: Iran Offers to Reopen Strait of Hormuz if US Lifts Blockade; Trump Rejects Proposal

key_facts.fact: Iran proposed reopening the Strait of Hormuz in exchange for the US lifting its blockade and ending the war, while deferring nuclear negotiations for later.
Araghchi conducted a 72-hour diplomatic sprint visiting Pakistan (twice), Oman (Muscat), and Russia (meeting Putin in St. Petersburg) to secure broader buy-in for the plan.
Trump told advisers he is not satisfied with Iran's latest ceasefire proposal, according to a US official.
Trump faces a May 1 deadline under the War Powers Resolution to obtain congressional authorization to continue military operations against Iran, now in their ninth week.
Araghchi also spoke by phone with foreign ministers of Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Egypt, and France over the past three days to brief them on ceasefire developments.

stories.headline: AI Photonics Chipmaker Lightelligence Surges 408% in Hong Kong IPO Debut

key_facts.fact: Shanghai-based Lightelligence shares surged as much as 408% to HK$930 after pricing at HK$183.20 in its Hong Kong IPO debut.
The company raised about HK$2.5 billion (~$310M) in the IPO, making it one of the most explosive debuts in recent memory.
The retail tranche was oversubscribed 5,784.7 times, with cornerstone investors including Alibaba Investment, GIC, and Temasek subscribing to more than 71% of the offering.
Lightelligence makes optical interconnect and optical-computing products that use light instead of electronic pathways to move data in AI data centers, reducing latency and power use.
Frost & Sullivan forecasts the global AI computing and interconnect market will grow at a 27% compound annual rate through 2031.

stories.headline: Microsoft and OpenAI Overhaul Deal: End Exclusivity, Drop AGI Clause, Open Multi-Cloud Access

key_facts.fact: OpenAI can now serve all products across any cloud provider including AWS and Google Cloud, ending Microsoft's exclusivity as sole cloud provider
The controversial AGI clause has been eliminated; Microsoft now retains a non-exclusive IP license through a fixed date of 2032, regardless of technology progress
Microsoft will no longer pay any revenue share to OpenAI; OpenAI continues paying Microsoft 20% through 2030, now subject to a total cap
The restructuring was driven by Amazon's $50B investment in OpenAI and $100B AWS cloud commitment, which conflicted with the original Microsoft exclusivity
Amazon CEO Andy Jassy said OpenAI's models will be available on Bedrock 'in the coming weeks' alongside the Stateful Runtime Environment
Microsoft retains approximately 27% ownership of OpenAI's for-profit entity and reported $7.5B in revenue from its OpenAI investment in a single quarter

stories.headline: Nvidia Sets All-Time Market Cap Record at $5.26 Trillion After 4% Surge

key_facts.fact: Nvidia's market capitalization hit $5.26 trillion on Monday April 27, the highest ever for a publicly traded company, after a 4% share price jump.
Nvidia shares are now up 16% year-to-date after slumping in March.
The rally was driven by the ongoing data center boom and AI infrastructure spending by hyperscalers.
Nvidia currently trades at roughly 24x forward earnings, a discount to customers like Broadcom (35x) despite having the strongest competitive moat in the semiconductor stack.

stories.headline: OpenAI Missed Internal Revenue and 1B Weekly User Target, CFO Worried About Paying Compute Contracts

key_facts.fact: OpenAI missed an internal goal of reaching 1 billion weekly active ChatGPT users by the end of 2025
OpenAI missed its annual revenue target for ChatGPT last year and multiple monthly revenue targets in early 2026, as Anthropic surged in enterprise markets
CFO Sarah Friar told company leaders she is worried OpenAI might not be able to pay for future computing contracts if revenue doesn't grow fast enough
Friar has also expressed reservations about OpenAI's plans to go public by the end of 2026
OpenAI-linked stocks fell on the news: CoreWeave down 5.4%, Oracle down 5.5%, AMD and Broadcom both off roughly 4% in premarket trading

stories.headline: OpenAI Releases Symphony, Open-Source Agent Orchestrator That Turns Issue Trackers Into Coding Agent Control Planes

key_facts.fact: Symphony is an open-source orchestration layer that connects project management tools like Linear to Codex agents, assigning a dedicated agent workspace to each open issue
Some OpenAI teams saw a 500% increase in landed pull requests during the first three weeks of using Symphony
The repo has already accumulated 15,500 stars on GitHub since its quiet launch last month
OpenAI built an internal productivity tool with no human-written code, using the Symphony approach where every open issue gets a Codex agent
Symphony is positioned as a reference implementation, not a standalone product; OpenAI encourages teams to fork and rebuild it for their own needs

stories.headline: South Korea Surpasses UK to Become World's 8th-Largest Stock Market at $4.04 Trillion

key_facts.fact: South Korea's total stock market capitalization jumped 45% this year to $4.04 trillion, surpassing the UK's $3.99 trillion to become the world's 8th-largest market.
The KOSPI broke the 6,700 threshold for the first time on an intraday basis, closing at 6,641.02, up 0.39% from the previous session.
Samsung Electronics and SK hynix account for more than 40% of KOSPI's total market capitalization, driving the AI-linked chip rally.
The UK market was about twice the size of Korea's as recently as 2024, but the gap reversed in just over a year.
Analysts forecast KOSPI could reach 7,100-7,900 based on forward PE normalization, with corporate governance reforms under President Lee Jae Myung providing additional support.

stories.headline: South Korea Surpasses UK as World's 8th-Largest Stock Market, Driven by Samsung and SK Hynix

key_facts.fact: South Korea's total stock market value has jumped more than 45% in 2026 to about $4.04 trillion, surpassing the UK's roughly $3.99 trillion to become the world's eighth-largest equity market.
Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix make up more than 40% of the Kospi index's total value, concentrating the rally in AI-linked semiconductor stocks.
Taiwan also recently overtook the UK to become the world's seventh-largest equity market at around $4.48 trillion, driven largely by TSMC.
The ranking shift reflects how market size is increasingly a supply-chain scoreboard, set by who controls critical links in global tech supply chains.

stories.headline: ULA Atlas V Launches 29 Amazon Kuiper Satellites, Ties Heaviest Payload Record

key_facts.fact: A United Launch Alliance Atlas V rocket launched 29 Amazon Kuiper broadband internet satellites from Cape Canaveral on April 27 at 8:53 PM EDT.
This was ULA's 6th flight delivering production Amazon Kuiper satellites and its 7th overall, with the launch tying the Atlas V record for heaviest payload ever flown.
ULA completed its second Atlas V launch of the month, marking the company's fastest turnaround at Space Launch Complex 41 to date.
This was the 108th launch of an Atlas V overall and the 100th under ULA. All 29 satellites were confirmed deployed.
SpaceX also attempted a Falcon Heavy launch of the final ViaSat-3 satellite on the same day but scrubbed due to poor weather.

stories.headline: US Data Center Pipeline Hits 780 GW — Exceeding National Peak Load — as Rural Communities Push Back

key_facts.fact: There are 780 gigawatts of announced data center projects in the US, exceeding the country's current total peak load of 759 GW, according to Aurora Energy Research.
EPC firm McCarthy Building Companies says construction timelines for data centers have tripled from 6 months to 18 months, and estimates only one in four queued projects is real.
Grid Strategies quadrupled its earlier prediction to 166 GW of peak demand growth over the next five years, with about 90 GW tied to data centers specifically.
Pew data shows 67% of planned data centers are in rural areas, while 87% of existing ones are in urban areas, and many rural communities are 'viscerally opposed' to AI infrastructure.
In Archbald, Pennsylvania (population ~7,000), residents are pushing back against six proposed data center campuses that would cover about 14% of the town's land.
Aurora Energy Research modeled adding 10 GW of data center load in ERCOT without new transmission and found it would quintuple congestion costs and spike power prices by 34%.

stories.headline: Xiaomi Open-Sources MiMo-V2.5 Trillion-Parameter Models Under MIT License, Rivals Frontier Models

key_facts.fact: Xiaomi released MiMo-V2.5-Pro (1.02T total params, 42B active) and MiMo-V2.5 (310B total params, 15B active) under the MIT License with 1M context window
MiMo-V2.5-Pro leads the open-source field with 63.8% success rate on ClawEval benchmarks, using ~70K tokens per trajectory — 40-60% fewer tokens than Claude Opus 4.6, Gemini 3.1 Pro, and GPT-5.4
The Pro model achieved 1581 on GDPVal-AA (Elo) benchmark, surpassing Kimi K2.6 and GLM 5.1
V2.5-Pro autonomously implemented a complete SysY compiler in Rust in 4.3 hours (672 tool calls, 233/233 on test suites) and built an 8,192-line video editor in 11.5 hours
API pricing: Pro at $1.00/M input tokens, $3.00/M output (≤256K context); base model at $0.40/M input, $2.00/M output, making them among the cheapest frontier-class models
Xiaomi is offering developers and creators 100 trillion free tokens to build with the models
